questions.question_html: Which property of $CO_{2}$ makes it biologically and geo-chemically important?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.html: Its low solubility in water

options.label: C

questions.explanation_text: The property of low solubility of carbon dioxide in water makes it biologically and geo-chemically important. Carbon dioxide on reaction with water form carbonic acid, which dissociates to give $HCO_{3}^{-}$ ions. $H_{2}CO_{3}/HCO_{3}^{-}$ buffer system helps to maintain $pH$ of blood between $7.26-7.42$ .

questions.question_text:
The volume of $2.8g$ of $CO$ at $27^{\circ}C$ and 0.821 atm pressure is
( $R=0.08210\text{L. atm K}mol^{-1}$ )
questions.question_html: The volume of $2.8g$ of $CO$ at $27^{\circ}C$ and 0.821 atm pressure is ( $R=0.08210\text{L. atm K}mol^{-1}$ )
questions.explanation_text: Given, amount of $CO=2.8g$ Temperature $=27^{\circ}C$ Pressure $=0.821atm$ $R=0.08210LatmKmol^{-1}$ We know that, $pV=RT$ $\therefore V=\frac{RT}{p}=\frac{0.0821 \times 300}{0.821}=30L$ $\therefore 28g$ of CO occupy volume $30L$ $\therefore 2.8g$ of CO occupy volume $=\frac{30 \times 2.8}{28}=3L$
questions.explanation_html:
Given, amount of $CO=2.8g$

Temperature $=27^{\circ}C$

Pressure $=0.821atm$

$R=0.08210LatmKmol^{-1}$

We know that, $pV=RT$

$\therefore V=\frac{RT}{p}=\frac{0.0821 \times 300}{0.821}=30L$

$\therefore 28g$ of CO occupy volume $30L$

$\therefore 2.8g$ of CO occupy volume $=\frac{30 \times 2.8}{28}=3L$

questions.question_text: Which of the following equations does not represent Charles's law for a given mass of gas at constant pressure?
questions.question_html: Which of the following equations does not represent Charles's law for a given mass of gas at constant pressure?
questions.explanation_text: Charle's law states that "pressure remaining constant, the volume of a fixed mass of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. The general equation is as follows : $\frac{V}{T}=\text{Constant}(K);V=KT\text{.... (i)}$ Taking the logarithm of equation (i) $\begin{aligned} & logV=logK+logT\text{.... (ii)} \\ & logK=logV-logT\text{.... (iii)} \end{aligned}$ Equation (ii) can also be represented as $lnV=lnK+lnT\text{.... (iv)}$ Taking differentiation of equation (iv) w.r.t $T$ . $\frac{d(lnV)}{dT}=0+\frac{1}{T};\frac{d(lnV)}{dT}=\frac{1}{T}$
questions.explanation_html:
Charle's law states that "pressure remaining constant, the volume of a fixed mass of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. The general equation is as follows :

$\frac{V}{T}=\text{Constant}(K);V=KT\text{.... (i)}$

Taking the logarithm of equation (i)

$\begin{aligned} & logV=logK+logT\text{.... (ii)} \\ & logK=logV-logT\text{.... (iii)} \end{aligned}$

Equation (ii) can also be represented as

$lnV=lnK+lnT\text{.... (iv)}$

Taking differentiation of equation (iv) w.r.t $T$ .

$\frac{d(lnV)}{dT}=0+\frac{1}{T};\frac{d(lnV)}{dT}=\frac{1}{T}$

questions.question_text: For an ideal gas, compressibility factor is
questions.question_html: For an ideal gas, compressibility factor is
questions.explanation_text: The compressibility factor, denoted by $Z$ , is defined as: $Z=\frac{PV}{nRT}$ For an ideal gas, the ideal gas law states that: $PV=nRT$ Substituting this into the expression for $Z$ gives: $Z=\frac{nRT}{nRT}=1$ So, the compressibility factor for an ideal gas is 1. Answer: Option B.
questions.explanation_html:
The compressibility factor, denoted by $Z$ , is defined as:

$Z=\frac{PV}{nRT}$

For an ideal gas, the ideal gas law states that:

$PV=nRT$

Substituting this into the expression for $Z$ gives:

$Z=\frac{nRT}{nRT}=1$

So, the compressibility factor for an ideal gas is 1.

Answer: Option B.

questions.explanation_text: Dry ice is the solid form of carbon dioxide. Here's a quick explanation: Dry ice is made of carbon dioxide ( $CO_{2}$ ). At atmospheric pressure, carbon dioxide does not melt into a liquid but instead transitions directly from a solid to a gas; this process is called sublimation. Among the options provided, the correct answer is the one that indicates dry ice is a solid form of carbon dioxide. Thus, the correct answer is: Option C: solid $CO_{2}$
